Results:

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ykvPr2oC219g1XZI0rBkyej-_E5sCUoT4Ow20jnT6zw/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ykvPr2oC219g1XZI0rBkyej-_E5sCUoT4Ow20jnT6zw/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] 

Query:

{noformat}SELECT
  country,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ffr.user_id) AS users,
  SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur + lifetime_1y_flv_gmv_eur) AS sum_1y_gmv_predicted_eur,
  SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_gmv_eur) as sum_1y_gmv_actual,
  SUM(lifetime_1y_hlv_profit_simplified_eur + lifetime_1y_flv_profit_simplified_eur) AS sum_1y_profit_simplified_eur
FROM
  ng_public.etl_first_finished_ride_for_user AS ffr
  -- using left join to take all existing users (not only those who have LTVs)
LEFT JOIN
  ng_public.etl_rider_predicted_ltv_aggregated AS ltv
ON
  ffr.user_id = ltv.user_id
WHERE
  --campaign_code = ‘SOLYPLAYA’
country = ‘Spain’
and created_date between date(‘2022-07-01’) and date(‘2022-09-01’)
GROUP BY 1{noformat}

* 6.2 objectives monitoring, measurement and evaluation – ongoing
* 9.2 Internal audits – ongoing
* 9.3 management reviews – ongoing

* Annex A 5 – reviews of policies – ongoing
* Annex A 7 – human resource engagement and awareness
* Annex A 16 – security incidents, events and weaknesses – ongoing

* General external audits (eg for UKAS certification by ISO certified bodies)

Improvements can also come from many other places and it is to be encouraged that they get documented within the ISMS improvement process. These include:

* Customers requests or concerns

Hi [~accountid:632d88e0748d1bfcb858128d],

We have section 3.4 dealing with logos and branding in Driver T&Cs: 
_3.4. Using tags and labels of Bolt. Additionally, we may give you tags, labels, stickers or other signs that refer to Bolt brand or otherwise indicate you are using the Bolt Platform. We grant you a non-exclusive, non-sublicensable, non-transferable license to use such signs and only for the purpose of indicating you are providing Transportation Services via the Bolt Platform. After termination of the Agreement you must immediately remove and discard any signs that refer to Bolt brand._

Based on the information provided by you, I understand we may request removal of the branding with fleets / drivers where (i) the contract has been terminated (hereafter referred to as +Scenario A+) or (ii) the contract is still valid but the fleet / driver has failed to provide sufficient proof of the branding or removal of the branding (hereafter referred to as +Scenario B+) . Is this understanding correct? 

*Scenario A* 

If the contract with the fleet / driver has been terminated, i.e. they no longer use the Bolt platform to provide transportation services, then we can rely on the T&C section 3.4 referred to above. The fleet / driver has an obligation to remove branding if the agreement has been terminated. If the fleet / driver does not do this then they are in breach of the T&Cs and we can therefore claim damages from them for such breach and enforcement of the removal of the branding by bringing legal action. This would however incur costs for Bolt and therefore this is generally not done but we can always inform the fleets / drivers of such possibility in order to get the to act. I suggest that a template response is drafted for such cases where our request and position is clarified. 

*Scenario B* 

This scenarios is not explicitly covered by the T&Cs as we have not terminated the contract. If the fleets / drivers to not provide sufficient proof of the branding / removal of branding, do we want to terminate the contract or do we only want to enforce removal of the branding? Do we want to be able to request removal of the branding at our sole discretion or only if the driver is disparaging Bolt? Please clarify the issues further in order for us to assess what the appropriate legal action would be.

Best regards, 

Michelle

[~accountid:6099349cb050a70069806a78] , I wonder if the difference between a proforma invoice and a prepayment invoice that you referred to in the document you shared is only a nomenclature matter or if there is any other difference. For tax and VAT purposes we think that the most suitable solution would be a *proforma invoice* because it does not trigger tax nor VAT effects. However, a “prepayment invoice” may give rise to the accrual of VAT at a different moment from the effective shipment of the assets, and such a circumstance may give rise to mismatches between VAT returns including these transactions and the Intrastat returns where we have to report them.

Regardless of the term we use to refer to this kind of invoice in our system, a proforma invoice will qualify as such as long as the document clearly shows the term "Proforma invoice" and the phrase "This is not a tax invoice". Therefore, it may be easier and quicker to create proforma invoices in WD than what might be initially thought. 

Thank you! Have a good day.

For coverage, from my review of this agreement these are the areas not covered and/or unclear, if you wish to proceed with this agreement we are bound by these terms:  

+*Issues with the lack of defined terms*+ 

The following definitions are not in the agreement

# Initial Minimum Term 
# Recorded Delivery 
# Term 
# Notice period

*As there is no definitions to these terms this may cause issues with interpretation of the agreement.*

+*Other matters to flag:*+

On the first page, point 15 under the definition ‘Fixed term’ it says “the licence agreement shall run until 31 May 2023” - *Is this an error and supposed to be 31 May 2024? if this is a typo I would advise requesting the date is corrected prior to signing.* 

Clause 14(e) is an indemnity clause, as standard business practice Bolt does not agree to indemnities. clause 14(e) says: _“Indemnify the Owner and its respective officers, employees and agents, from all claims, liability, or loss, and all damages and costs incurred by the Owner, which arise out of the use of the Accommodation and the Premises by the Client. The Client shall maintain adequate insurance against all such risks”_ - *Just want to flag that if Bolt does agree to indemnities it is preferred that the indemnity is drafted quite narrow in the sense that the other party should have a limit on the indemnity to only include losses that can be proven, this indemnity is not drafted in this way and is quite wide in scope as it says that Bolt will be indemnifying the Licensor “from all claims, liability, or loss, and all damages and costs incurred by the Owner” therefore there is no obligation for the Licensor to prove the losses and the amount is not capped and/or limited.* 

Clause 20 _“Where the Client comprises more than one individual such individuals shall be jointly and severally liable to observe and perform the Client’s obligations under the Licence”_

Clause 21 _“Where the Client comprises a Limited Liability Company or Partnership, the Directors or Partners who sign The Licence shall be jointly and severally liable to observe and perform and act as Guarantors of the Client’s obligations under The Licence”_

*I want to flag Clause 20 and Clause 21 as these clauses essentially mean that other people other than Bolt can be held liable under this Agreement. Essentially clause 21 is saying that the Directors who sign this Licence Agreement will be liable to ensure the obligations are met under the contract and they act as a guarantor. I would ensure that the director who will be signing this agreement is happy to proceed on the basis of clause 21 as it is a personal liability to the director so this should be brought to their attention prior to signing.* 

As previously discussed on this ticket, the clauses above are the clauses l flagged for us to try and amend with the Licensor, however it seems the Licensor is not willing to enter into discussions about amending any of the Licence Agreement. 

From a legal standpoint I would prefer for these clauses to be amended so they are not slanted in favour of the Licensor and are more balanced for Bolt. However, I appreciate that we have limited options with the offices that are available in Milton Keynes. Taking the above into consideration, [~accountid:60420da05290e70069b64add] please let me know if you are happy to proceed and be bound by the above terms.

I think we should push back on Santander being able to terminate the lease upon any breach whatsoever. I doubt they will exercise this in practice but I don’t see why we should give them the leverage. Perhaps it would be worth adding a comment along the following lines: 

_“While we understand that Santander is a professional Lessor and we do not envisage that Santander would abuse the broad termination rights granted to it by this Agreement, we must push back on Santander having the right to terminate the Agreement upon just any breach whatsoever. This would give the Lessor the right to terminate the lease even in case the Lessee would fail to notify the Santander about a change in address. Not only would this put the Lessee’s entire business at a risk which no diligent entrepreneur can accept, but it would also make it difficult for the Lessee to raise any funds from investors. Therefore, even if the Lessee can rely on Santander being a reasonable Lessor and not abusing its broad termination rights, the fact that Santander has such broad termination rights is a risk in itself which might impair the Lessee’s ability to raise financing. That said, in our experience, it is common that a lessor would be able to terminate a lease only in case the lessee has breached the agreement in a manner which has material impact to the lessor’s interests. Therefore, we do not see why Santander should oppose its termination right being limited to material breach.”_

We could then add the following Section for Santander’s comfort: _“The Lessee not having paid any amounts due under this Agreement in 10 business days as of having received a respective notice from SC Renting shall be deemed a material breach of the lease contract which shall grant SC Renting the right to terminate the lease contract._

Sure! So:

* Churns → driver hasn’t taken any orders for 30 days

Let’s say we have a driver who took the last order on 1st May → we add 30 days to this (so 31st May) and this will be the churn detected date

* Reactivation → driver hasn’t taken  any orders for 30 days but then decided to take another ride

Following the example above, we’ve detected churn for this driver on 31st May & let’s say the driver took another order on 1st June. This means the driver is currently active (as today is 13th June) but during May they were churned hence we count as 1. 

* Reactivation Rate → how many drivers in total have re-activated as of today vs total drivers who’ve churned

Let’s start with a simple explanation of the differences. The fraud calculations are very dynamic and review each individual, their history and behaviour individually. This means that based on the information available to us from the user, a similar report or issue can have different restrictions and outcomes. Another factor that can be at play is the time itself. Not only do we look at users themself but also certain external indicators to go with the internal indicators.

You can also think this way. We have built the risk indicators and score in a way that users with lower risk are able to escape the limitations through the verification and with high risk or high accumulated risk, we have decided not to let the users pass regardless of the verification. Further, keep in mind that the rules and restrictions are smart - some users will not be able to use our services as we are seeing distinct fraud flags. In those cases, there is nothing to do but to advise that the service is not available to them at this time. 

If you strongly believe that a user should be able to order and they are good, have followed through with all the required steps (like verification) and are still restricted, you may bring it up with us as an example. Bear in mind that we need to have a detailed description of what makes you believe so. In general, we do not look at users on an individual level. 

Out of the examples you have provided only one has completed verification, hence, the recommendation is to continue there first with them. We do not see anything afloat with the provided cases.

Hey [~accountid:60b0a48fd435380069b90208] !

The situation in markets is different, but in LT we have the lowest reclassification risk out of the three Baltic states (reclassification risk in the whole Baltic region is law, too). Although the assessment was made for LT RH, findings are applicable alto to BF because the law and legal principles are the same. Below is the short summary that equally applies to drivers and couriers:

* Lithuanian State Labour and Tax Inspectorates both have the right to re-classify civil relations between a company and natural person into employment relations. 
* The relations are assessed based on their true economic substance through a "substance over form" approach. There is no concrete rule as to how many criteria should be met before establishing an employment relationship.
* Usage of statistical blocking increases the strength of the argument that drivers/couriers are under authority of Bolt and must comply with its procedure of work. However, *many other attributes can be assessed as more leaning towards civil relations* such as pay of the driver/courier depends on results, drivers/couriers take the risk for damages, drivers/couriers plan their own work time, drivers/couriers are not provided with a workplace, drivers/couriers are responsible for paying their own taxes, no agreements regarding leave or similar are concluded, etc.
* There is *no practice* of Lithuanian authorities to take action in re-classifying relations between labour platforms and their workers in Lithuania. Thus, *the risk of re-classification before the adoption of the Directive remains much lower.* But once the EU Platform Workers Directive is adopted, and transported into the national law (within 2-3 years), Labour/ Tax authorities would become more active and will launch their own inspections, because the Directive will create a legal presumption of an employment relationship between platforms and persons performing platform work.  Since the Directive will be applicable in all of the EU, possibly in 2-3 years we would need to stop using statistical blocking in all of the EU.

Based on the above, it is ok to block some couriers if after warning their behaviour is not improved.  Setting an adequate threshold makes total sense because we need to take care of our user comfort and satisfaction with the use of Bolt services. Hope it answers your question 🙂

h1. Is conversion data gathered correctly?

There are two metrics which we use to calculate conversion: {{otp_snet_verify}} metric (incremented when an SMS is sent) and {{sms_conversion_tracking}} (incremented when OTP code was used). If any of the above metrics were incorrectly gathered, then it would influence our graphs.


*Hypotesis:* {{otp_sent_verify}} metrics are pumped-up by microservices other than {{one-time-password}}
*Check*: No other micorservice uses the {{conversion_tracking_support}} flag in our code. Hence, {{otp_sent_verify}} metrics are incremented only when {{one-time-password}} sends an SMS.



*Hypotestis:* {{sms_otp_verified}} events are not sent to the queue, hence {{sms_conversion_tracking}} metrics are not incremented.
*Check*: Events are being sent to the queue properly - [the amount of messages|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/000000011/aws-sqs?orgId=1&var-Datasource=CloudWatch&var-region=eu-central-1&var-queue=otp-conversion-publisher&from=now-28d&to=now&viewPanel=7]



*Hypotesis:* {{sms_otp_verified}} events are consumed with a big delay, hence {{sms_conversion_tracking}} metrics are incremented with delay, which corrupts our conversation percentage
*Check*:  Queue serves the events in a timely manner - the messages do not pile-up. We sometimes experience a tiny delay, but it’s up to 14 seconds (so our conversation metrics should not be corrupted because of that) - [amount of old messages|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/000000011/aws-sqs?orgId=1&var-Datasource=CloudWatch&var-region=eu-central-1&var-queue=otp-conversion-publisher&from=now-28d&to=now&viewPanel=1] 



*Hypotestis:* {{sms_otp_verified}} events are sent to the queue on the wrong conversion state, which means that we increment {{sms_conversion_tracking}} metrics in scenarios, when we should not.
*Check:* Events are sent to a queue only after the first usage of OTP code (status: {{OtpState.VERIFIED}})



*Conclusion: We gather both metrics in timely manner. We count only requests from* {{one-time-password}}*. All confirmation sms sent attempts and all verified SMS OTP codes are processed when they should.*

Hey!

* Re: recording the calls - as per our guidelines that you also brought out, we need to mention the fact of the recording in order to be compliant and there is no compliant workaround for that, unfortunately. At the same time, if you make sure that the recordings are stored for a short time and the access is very limited, then it is probably not a very high risk (yet not compliant with the rules, as mentioned).

Then there are couple other privacy related issues here I would like to bring out

* If you are using a third party in order to collect the numbers, such as [apollo.io|http://apollo.io], then we need to make sure we have a legal basis to collect these numbers and there are contractual safeguards in place (recommend to create another ticket on this, if this has not been reviewed before)
* We also need to be sure of the legality of making these calls - this usually depends on whether it is a business contact or personal phone number. The rules on this are specific to each country, so they need to be assessed separately. Per my assessment (not as local law expert) 

# *UK* - Telemarketing is opt-out, which means we can make the calls for people who have not opted-out from this. Furthermore, the Corporate Telephone Preference Service (CTPS) register and a similar register for fax preference (FPS) are in place for named individuals who do not wish to receive these communications. 
# *PT* - We can make the calls for people who have not opted-out from this. There is a list called the “Robinson” list which is an _Opt-out_ System based on a list of consumers who do not want to receive advertisements and have asked to be included on the Robinson list.
# *RO -* We can make the calls for people who have not opted-out from this. Romania does not have a national "do-not-call list".

From bigger countries, it seems like in *Germany*, we need a consent or opt-in for conducting such calls. 

Let me know, if you would like to receive an opinion on some other country or would like to conduct a more thorough legal analysis with the help of a local expert.

# _Is the current passenger consent stance appropriate?_

Currently our stance is when we receive a complaint from a customer regarding a Ride, we advise the Council of the complaint and provide details of the Driver who is related to the complaint. We do not provide Rider details unless we garner their consent.

Our approach is correct. We have a duty to the Rider under GDPR to protect their personal data. Our licensing agreement, nor the conditions of our agreement, take precedence over our GDPR obligations.

We are meeting the conditions of our licensing agreement as best we can while under the obligations of GDPR. We also need to be mindful that by advising the Rider that reporting an issue to us will result in a report to the Council being generated, and their details being shared, we would discourage people to report complaints in the first instance.

Under GDPR we require a legal basis to provide their details and the only appropriate legal basis in this instance is consent.

2. _Do we intend to introduce T&Cs re passenger consent? Can we introduce them in the upcoming T&Cs change on 1 July?_

We are not able to include consent of this type within our T&Cs are suggested in our previous call.

3. _What remedies do we have against the officer circumnavigating our privacy safeguards?_

We do not have much in terms of remedies therefore an emphasis must be placed on prevention over remedy. Any request for personal data which there is any doubt on how to handle then please continue to reach out to Privacy to access.

Hi [~accountid:628dd71f1c97b5006f0b7f05], thanks for your feedback below.

*Need for a Data Processing Agreement*

In short, Bolt +cannot+ outsource these activities (which involve personal data processing) to a third party without having a binding agreement in place that regulates what that third party does with the Driver data, and which requires the third party to comply with data protection law (including Kenyan law). This is typically done via a _Data Processing Agreement_.

We do not currently have a Data Processing Agreement that I can provide to you which allows for customisation to Kenyan/African laws, however, this is on our agenda and soon we will be in a position to provide one to you. I also note that Picktime’s Privacy Policy is very light-touch and it does not appear to have a customer-facing data processing agreement of its own, which does not reflect well on its privacy compliance programme.

*Consequences of engaging Picktime without a Data Processing Agreement*:

# Engaging Picktime without the necessary privacy documentation in place would automatically render Bolt in breach of Kenya’s data protection law.
# Because Picktime is based in the USA (Texas), use of its services by Bolt will involve transfers of personal data outside of Kenya to a foreign country. The Data Processing Agreement would need to include provisions that ensure that Picktime complies with Kenyan data protection law when transferring data to the USA.

*Alternative - Goodtime?*
In the interim, you may want to consider reaching out to [~accountid:6268ef7d0f0cc0006f8f1e23] about Bolt’s existing relationship with [Goodtime|https://goodtime.io/], who currently provides the same functionality for Bolt’s interview scheduling. We would recommend leveraging an existing relationship with a known supplier who has been onboarded and preferably had contracts reviewed by legal and privacy (this is currently in progress for the Goodtime contract renewal - [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-19905?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYzFmMGNhZGIzYTAxNGFjZTgzOWFjNWM5YjVmNDczOTQiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-19905?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYzFmMGNhZGIzYTAxNGFjZTgzOWFjNWM5YjVmNDczOTQiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link]). This would also save costs for Bolt and your Business line. [~accountid:6268ef7d0f0cc0006f8f1e23] may be able to advise on (or put you onto someone else who can advise) whether Bolt Kenya could use Bolt’s existing subscription for its Driver Centre appointments, or whether Bolt Kenya would be required to enter into its own Order for a license (which your Legal team can help facilitate).

If you were to proceed with Goodtime, we would still need to introduce certain ‘local’ amendments to the Goodtime DPA to cater for Kenyan law so please keep me updated as to how you will be proceeding so that I can prepare these amendments.

Hey [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] please see the analysis below. Please pay attention to the parts in bold about EE.

*LITHUANIA* 

# *Reclassification of Bolt drivers as employees.* It may be possible to argue that due to the level of involvement in the Campaign branding situation, self-employed Bolt drivers could be classified as employees. However, +we did not identify that Campaign branding service would increase such risk.+ +This would still be treated as provision of services and not labour relations.+
# *Tax-related actions for drivers.* In case of Pure advertising situation, self-employed Bolt drivers could be treated as providing advertising services to Bolt in addition to the driving services which are provided through Bolt’s platform. This +from the drivers’ perspective may require additional registration or declaration that such services are provided with the Tax Inspectorate.+ However, f+rom Bolt’s perspective, this should not raise any tax-related risks.+ For drivers this shouldn’t also bear any negative consequences as all self-provided services are taxed in the same manner.
# *General advertising requirements*. As new branding terms would not introduce any significant changes to Bolt’s advertising practices, we see no issues there. Generally, +all advertisement is allowed unless it contradicts good morality or public order+ (except for specifically regulated sectors, such as alcohol or tobacco, where more strict requirements or complete prohibitions apply). This is not the case here.

*LATVIA*

# *Reclassification of Bolt drivers as employees*. Legal rules for qualifying engaged individuals as employees are quite strict in Latvia. +Already now even without advertising, there may be arguments that due to the level of involvement the self-employed Bolt drivers may potentially be classified as employees.+ However, the proposed +advertising services as such do not seem to increase the risk+ as some level of risk persists regardless of advertising services provided.
# *Tax-related actions for drivers*. In case of Pure advertising situation, self-employed Bolt drivers could be treated as providing advertising services to Bolt in addition to the driving services which are provided through Bolt’s platform. +For drivers this should not cause any negative consequences as all self-provided services are taxed in the same manner and the main activity remains unchanged+. Also, +from Bolt’s perspective, this should not raise any tax-related risks.+
# *General advertising requirements.* In most cases, all types of advertisements are allowed as long as they don't go against good morals or public order. As new branding terms would not introduce any significant changes to Bolt’s advertising practices, we see no issues there. +Placing advertisements in public areas or places visible to the public usually need permission from the relevant municipality+. However, this permission i+s not necessary, if the advertisement is painted or attached as a sticker on a privately-owned vehicle+, if it is not a separate structure specifically built for advertising purposes (known as a mobile advertisement).

*ESTONIA* 

# *Reclassification of Bolt drivers as employees.* The risk of reclassification of drivers as employees remains and it would increase if the new contracts affected the independence of the drivers. *Any guidelines by Bolt to the drivers regarding the method, time or place of their work could affect the level of degree of the driver’s independence*. The independence in turn is a critical indicator when evaluating whether the driver is an employee or a service provider. In addition, *the risk could increase if Bolt supervises the drivers, requires them to act in a certain way, prescribes sanctions (e.g. regarding work time, the option to accept rides, use subcontractors) for infringements etc.* European Council has just made a press release (available [here|https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2023/06/12/rights-for-platform-workers-council-agrees-its-position/#:~:text=It%20aims%20to%3A,labour%20and%20social%20protection%20rights]) according to which the Council has agreed to start negotiations with the European Parliament on the Platform Workers Directive. Please note that we have not analyzed the potential effect of this directive. The directive could prescribe that the platform and the person working through the platform (driver) conclude an employment agreement, if the platform controls certain elements of work. Although +we do not anticipate that the new branding terms will critically reduce the independence of the drivers, but we suggest that the new terms are carefully tested against the above criteria.+
# *Tax-related actions for drivers.* Regarding the tax implications of the advertising services: note that depending on the tax status of the driver, +the fees payable to the driver (either directly or by set-off against the commission fees) may be subject to withholding of personal income tax and payment of social tax by Bolt+. This likely requires additional analysis, as, according to our knowledge, the tax status of Estonian Bolt drivers may vary – they may operate in self-employed status or via a company, or, perhaps most often, by using the entrepreneur account regime. +The exact tax obligations of Bolt as the recipient of the service will depend on the exact status of the respective driver.+ The above is based on the assumption that the nature of the service is in fact provision of advertising and this change in the branding terms is not tax-driven.
# *General advertising requirements.* Similarly to Latvia and Lithuania, all advertising must be in accordance with the general requirements of the Advertising Act, incl. good moral, customs etc. In Estonia, local governmental authorities also have their individual legislation which regulates advertising on their territory. For example, Tallinn does not require a permit for placing stickers on a car. In addition to the advertising requirements, *we recommend clearly regulating the practical side of using Bolt’s brand. For example, the use of stickers. Contracts should include the process of placement and removal of the stickers, e.g., who is responsible for that, or who pays for that (we have encountered respective disputes in our practice).* *The risk here is having the car damaged if the placing or removal is not done correctly. Even correct removal may cause damages if the sticker has not been placed correctly.*

Bank transfers are payments that happen outside the Bolt payment ecosystem. We cannot support unofficial payment method issues with CS procedures because:

** _5.6 Bolt only encourages the use of 2 modes of payments i.e Cash payment and the in-App payment (Card) Bolt bears no liability on damages that may occur outside the outlined acceptable payment methods._
* If the rider has issues with their bank transfer, there’s really nothing much we can do on our side - they have to contact their bank.
* It is the driver’s responsibility to collect the money from the rider - if they selected cash, it should be paid in cash.

{code:sql}SELECT
	k.key,
	TRUNCATE(card_age_in_days, -1) as card_age_bins,
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.user_id) AS count_of_users,
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
	SUM(k.order_price) AS sum_of_in_app_orders_eur,
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
	SUM(k.fraud_amount) AS sum_of_fraud_payments_eur,
	(COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.0)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
	(SUM(k.fraud_amount) * 1.0) / SUM(k.order_price) AS fraud_payment_sum_ratio
FROM
	(
	select
		etl.created,
		etl.order_id AS orders_id,
		etl.user_price_eur AS order_price,
		etl.card_country AS card_country,
		etl.card_country || ':' || etl.country_code AS KEY,
		etl.country_code AS country_code,
		etl.user_id AS user_id,
		date_diff('day', ppmc.created_date, etl.created_date) as card_age_in_days,
		CASE
			WHEN etl.is_chargeback
			OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id
			ELSE NULL
		END AS fraud_payments,
		CASE
			WHEN etl.is_chargeback
			OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.user_price_eur
			ELSE NULL
		END AS fraud_amount
	FROM
		ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
		left join ng_public_spark.payment_payment_method_creation as ppmc on ppmc.payment_method_id = etl.payment_method_id
	WHERE
		etl.order_try_state = 'finished'
		AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
		AND etl.created >= DATEADD(month, -3, CURRENT_DATE)

	COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) AS count_of_in_app_orders,
	SUM(k.order_price) AS sum_of_in_app_orders_eur,
	COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) AS count_of_fraud_payments,
	SUM(k.fraud_amount) AS sum_of_fraud_payments_eur,
	(COUNT(DISTINCT k.fraud_payments) * 1.0)/ COUNT(DISTINCT k.orders_id) AS fraud_payment_count_ratio,
	(SUM(k.fraud_amount) * 1.0) / SUM(k.order_price) AS fraud_payment_sum_ratio,
	count(k.card_bin) as count_card_bin
FROM
	(
	SELECT
		etl.order_id AS orders_id,
		etl.user_price_eur AS order_price,
		etl.card_issuer AS card_issuer,
		etl.card_issuer || ':' || etl.country_code AS KEY,
		etl.country_code AS country_code,
		etl.user_id AS user_id,
		etl.card_bin as card_bin,
		date_diff('day', ppmc.created_date, etl.created_date) as card_age_in_days,
		CASE
			WHEN etl.is_chargeback
			OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.order_id
			ELSE NULL
		END AS fraud_payments,
		CASE
			WHEN etl.is_chargeback
			OR etl.is_payment_problem THEN etl.user_price_eur
			ELSE NULL
		END AS fraud_amount
	FROM
		ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
		left join ng_public_spark.payment_payment_method_creation as ppmc on ppmc.payment_method_id = etl.payment_method_id
	WHERE

		AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
		AND etl.created >= DATEADD(month, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
		AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(month, -3, CURRENT_DATE)
		and ppmc.created_date < etl.created_date
		and etl.card_country <> etl.country_code

The usual practise is that if the permanent location of the employee changes, so does the agreement: the old agreement is terminated (mutual agreement) and the new agreement is signed.

_If we have a cross-border agreement, then the situation gets a bit more complicated, as we have to follow the applicable law (location) and agreement legislation (EE) - this means, usually the more favorable conditions are applied, if not stated otherwise. If the employee has cross-border employment, there are some tax risks involved, that we would like to avoid (mostly - permanent establishment)._ 

* Tho, if the period is short, this can be regarded as business trip and I see no immediate danger (to the company). This means, we will have additional (tax free) cost of _per diem_.
* If he is travelling on his own accord and not fulfilling our instructions, I’d say the _per diem_ is not applicable as we allow working from abroad.   

On the whole, I’d consider the risks minimal for the company, as long as it is a short period and we have some audit trail of the agreement regarding him working abroad on his own accord.

Questions:

# Should the regular deferred (2h) delivery be supported along with regular and priority?

*Estimation notes (orchestration scope)*

In the City Assignment Builder and Delivery Order Planner the deferred-related settings are abstracted as {{DeferredSettingsProvider}}. So the change to support regular vs priority delivery might be limited to implementing a pair of new {{DeferredSettingsProvider}} implementations that would use some new (?)  or existing fields from the order record to determine whether an order should be treated as deferred and which settings (max ETA) should apply.

The trickier part might be the choice of a particular {{DeferredSettingsProvider}}, because we have quite a few cases to support and distinguish between already:

* regular deferred (2h) orders – those having {{dispatch_type: deferred}};
* provider-defined “deferred instant” orders – those coming from providers configured as “deferred instant” (*unless the city has per-eater deferred-instant enablement);*
* provider-and-user-defined “deferred instant”: in Bucharest there is a special city settings flag {{matching_settings.enable_deferred_instant_ab_test}} – in that case an order is considered deferred only if it’s both coming from deferred-instant-enabled provider *and* eater is enrolled into the AB test.

Besides that, existence of {{scheduled}} orders must be taken into account.

Action items:

The drivers can indeed issue invoices for transportation services without VAT if they are not VAT registered (VAT registration threshold is RON 300,000 a year, if drivers make less supplies then they are not required to register for VAT).

Bolt is buying these rides from the drivers and reselling these to business clients. Bolt is already VAT registered in Romania so we have to add VAT on all our invoices, no matter how we bought the rides ourselves or if we paid any VAT on that original purchase.

There is no reverse charge VAT applicable in Romania in this case. VAT is added to the invoice if the supplier is VAT registered and that’s it, there is no option of applying reverse charge (e.g adding 0% VAT to the invoice and have the business client declare the VAT itself).

Hope this clarifies it a bit.

About the Passive 4 weeks calculation. We check the current data and it is not following the rationale that we need for the metric. 
We need to change the measure in Looker since other departments use the metric in their reports and we need a singular place with the correct calculation. 

For this metric,
- We need to take clean the duplication of the  __exp ([https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DBA-263|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DBA-263])
- Exclude the delisted SKUs
- And consider the 4 weeks trend

How it should be calculated:
*- Unique SKUs Listed (4 weeks):* If the past 4 weeks the SKU was available in the session availability. We recommend using the session availability to exclude the delisted SKUs from the metric.
*- Unique SKU Sold (4 weeks):* If it had any sales in the last 4 weeks  and if also was  *Unique SKUs Listed (4 weeks)*, so we can avoid negative numbers in the Passive
*- Passive SKUs (4 weeks):   Unique SKUs Listed (4 weeks) -  Unique SKU Sold (4 weeks)*


Here you can find examples of how the calculation should work in a Google sheet.

{quote}So, if Food is AB-testing delivery fees and service fees for non-Bolt Market providers, and Bolt Market is AB-testing, say, MOV / Small Order Fee configs for Bolt Markets, the users will receive only one of two potential treatments.{quote}

This is how targeting works. [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3150873947/Priorities+between+Feature+Flags+Default+Parameters+and+AB+tests|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3150873947/Priorities+between+Feature+Flags+Default+Parameters+and+AB+tests|smart-link] 

A conflict happens between two entities (feature flags / tests / default parameters) if the following conditions are met:

* the two entities are active at the same time
* the two entities target the same actor (user / courier / provider / driver etc)
* the parameters of those two entities have at least a common key



h4. *Conflict resolution*

In the a/b testing system the following priorities as [defined in the config|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4af201f40a15e80aafb8d73a351ae33929216880/src/platform/abtest/targeting/main/config/config.defaults.production.ts#LL72C5-L72C28]:

Basically we are exposing an endpoint {{/some-api}} (supporting some filters + pagination) and expect

{{total_rows}}  is actually the count of the results held in {{data}}

🅰️ one endpoint for {{total_rows}}
🅱️ one for {{data}}

Here’s overall solution proposed by Infosec with some details still to be hashed out:

{quote}*Data obfuscation:* if I understand correctly, we want to run an analysis on this data, so encryption is off the table. We can use something called tokenization, in which we assign a unique token to each phone number in both our and partner’s phone number dataset while making sure same phone numbers have the same token. For this, we need to do some preprocessing on each dataset to make sure they are consistent and then run the same hashing algorithm on both datasets.

*Secure data transfer mechanism:* For this, the easiest way would be to use PGP. InfoSec team can help you with encrypting and decrypting the data with our company-wide PGP keypair. Please ask the partner for their public PGP key so we can securely encrypt all data to be sent so that only they can decrypt it with their private key. If the partner needs to send us data, let me know and I can give you our public PGP key to share with the partner. It would be best if we can discuss the details of this exchange with the partner as well.

*Expanding the set of data:* This is a bit challenging. I am assuming we can generate arbitrary phone numbers easily during the preprocessing stage. But then the question is how do _we_ distinguish between arbitrarily generated phone numbers and real ones. One way to do this would be to have two distinct datasets of real user phone numbers + arbitrarily generated phone numbers, tokenize them, merge them to send to partner. So only we know which are the real user phone numbers and which ones are not.{quote}

h3. Reference: Currency Exchange Rate Connector File Schema

[https://doc.workday.com/r/wsiU0cnNjCc_k7shLNxLEA/dB4D39i5pM3AkaTbNbzPuQ|https://doc.workday.com/r/wsiU0cnNjCc_k7shLNxLEA/dB4D39i5pM3AkaTbNbzPuQ]

h2. CSV File Format

||Column Name||Column Type||Description||
|_CalculateInverseRate_|_Boolean_|Select to calculate the inverse rates for the currency pairs included in the input file. This calculation enables you to reduce the cost of retrieving additional exchange rate data. You can also configure this value in the integration attributes.|
|_CalculateCrossRates_|_Boolean_|Select to calculate the cross rates between 2 currencies when you know the exchange rates of a common third currency. This calculation enables you to reduce the cost of retrieving exchange rate data. This value applies to the currency pairs you’ve included in the input file. You can also configure this value in the integration attributes.|
|_CrossRatesAnchorCurrency_|_String_|Select the currency you want to use as a reference when you calculate cross rates. You can also configure this value in the integration attribute.|
|_EffectiveTimestamp_|_DateTime_ or _Date_|Effective time stamp of the currency rate. Examples:
* 2011-01-01T00:00:00 (_DateTime_)
* 2011-01-01 (Date)|
|_FromCurrency_|_String_|Source currency name in ISO 4217 code format.|
|_TargetCurrency_|_String_|Target currency name in ISO 4217 code format.|
|_CurrencyRateType_|_String_|Currency rate type for the currency rate. Valid values:
* Average
* Budget
* Current
* Financial Budget
* Historic Equity
* Quarterly Average|
|_CurrencyRate_|_Decimal_|Currency rate value. Field supports up to 12 decimal precision.|

Hi Kunjal,

Couple thoughts here from my side, think Graeme’s team would own this from functional configuration side, but keen to get my input from a functional side also.

So the problem statement here lies: we receive revenue via customer invoices in Workday, from any revenue associated with the Bolt Drive business line, however this is actually being done where *additional charges* (outside of the normal car rental price) have occurred. This might be car damages, smoking inside the car, theft, parking tickets and so on. The current process is that these are manually communicated to finance, and then manual work on the finance side to get these input into the system as customer invoices and issued out to our Bolt Drive customers. They are currently booked to a singular customer *EE Bolt Drive customer (see: C-EE002-22-000393) and* the driver name, and car registration is input into the memo line. 

____

So if we are focusing on the automation of this, I think it is super important to state here that these would be for *additional charges* for existing Bolt Drive customers (personal accounts). I think using a generic customer e.g. EE Bolt Drive Customer is the right approach, as otherwise we would have to create thousands if not millions of customers who use the product, and that’s not maintainable. However here, I think we should specify a customer per each city that we operate in to allow us to have those worktags defaulting in. 

___

Additionally, potentially a separate ticket altogether may potentially be Bolt Business rental of these drive cars. 

___

So I think overall it’s a good idea, and I am really behind it to be able to map this out from the admin system, provide them with mapping of city=customer_ID, and the various sales items/revenue categories, then the worktags should default in auto based on the customer. Potentially could be looking at creating draft invoices so accountant can review this.

___

This is actually a fantastic use case for the O2C (Order to Cash) stream as part of Future Finance, and showing how we’re driving value in the process and system functionalities! 💪

*Summary of changes and demo configuration:*

+*Feature 1: Setup Required*+

Workday deliver these new web services that you can use to retrieve, record, or cancel multiple overpayments at once:

* Cancel Customer Overpayment (secured to the Process: Customer Overpayment - Cancel domain) 
* Get Customer Overpayments (secured to the Process: Customer Overpayment - View domain) 
* Submit Customer Overpayment (secured to the Customer Overpayment Event business process domain) 

!Screenshot 2023-03-08 at 2.27.01 PM.png|width=845,height=718!



_To process existing overpayments, they must be in Draft status. To process new overpayments, the related payment must have a status of:_

* _Applied with On-Account_
* _Approved_

+*Feature 2: Setup Not Required*+

To provide a consistent experience, when you use the new web service operations Workday now prevent you from canceling an overpayment if:

* It has been denied. 
* The associated payment is returned or unapplied.

Workday also prevent overpayment processing when:

* There's a refund in progress.
* There's a write-off in progress.
* The overpayment has been canceled.
* The associated payment has a journal in error.

[~accountid:6075604653cc020069760c71] Would you mind doing a peer review for me please, I will explain logic below and just want a second pair of eyes before I take it to the finance department and operations:

The business problem they have, is that they need a way of identifying different types of inventory usage to be able to determine the correct accounting. Majority of the inventory that we are used for scooter repairs, but the IOTs and Batteries are considered as part of the “whole” scooter which is then depreciated accordingly based on number of rides. 

The problem that has occured is we do not want to “double-book” the IOTs/Batteries under the expense accounts for spare parts AND depreciated, therefore when we went live with procurement, finance opted to use spend category Inventory Fixed Asset Components to do DR/CR to 1352 account for all these transactions. It does create lack of visibility, and business has come back saying that they actually use the IOTs/batteries for repair. 

After bit of research decided to use the *Custom Worktags* functionality, where I reconfigured Custom Worktag 07 to Inventory Usage Type and then configured the values accordingly (still pending business review). Through *Maintain Worktag Usage,* I added this as a required worktag on the Inventory Issue and Inventory Location objects. This is required for both quick issue and inventory issue/transfer tasks so it can be entered there for defaults, and driving accounting.

The system then let me configure Account Posting rules, with the condition rules selecting usage type to point to which account to go to. I was able to run a succesful test where I submitted an R9A IOT device, one for spare parts repair that went to account 1350, and upfitting which went to account 1352.

There is of course lots more testing and config required for the APR, but I think this is a viable solution, and I think the custom worktag is the best approach here. Do you agree [~accountid:6075604653cc020069760c71]?

thank you in advance 🙏

*Setup Effort:*

* On the Maintain Feature Opt-Ins report, opt in to the:
** Spend Authorization Routing for Workers with Multiple Positions feature.
** Expense Report Routing for Workers with Multiple Positions feature, if you haven't yet opted in.
* Grant the relevant security permissions to workers.

+What Happens If I Do Nothing:+

Thank you for the reminder. We have nothing clear to share yet. The tricky part is that currently this field is non-existent in our database. In the user interface it is calculated. So adding it to output document would require a bit more effort that it initially seemed. On the other hand when looking at a bigger picture and international standards (UBL2.1, EDIFACT etc) then field payment term might not only mean days in between invoice date and payment date. Other options are also supported. Current Telema eDoc standard also states that field type is NormalTextType (The string data type can contain characters, line feeds, carriage returns, and tab characters. Has lang attribute.)

We are currently trying to find a sustainable solution how we could share this info with Bolt AND not to end up a dead end during coming years when the meaning of payment term in the contexts of eFlow might get wider. Currently payment term is a numeric value displayed to the user in eFlow application. Currently it is always the result of following equation: due date - invoice date. Both dates are always present on eFlow's output. From my perspective it still seems a reliable solution to do this calculation somewhere in between Telema - Bolt connection - either on Telemas side or Bolts side. Please share once more your concerns why you did not want to do this calculation on your side.

More about eFlow features (might be irrelevant in this context): currently eFlow validates if this caluculated payment term matches with supplier payment term. This assumes on eFlow supplier card you have payment term. User interface will give a warning to user if payment term does not match with supplier data in eFlow. Validation is done currently only in "Lets flow status" and you must be an owner of the document to see the results. Currently this validation is not done for e-invoices, but this will change during few weeks done. All documents will be compared with supplier card data and mismatched will be highlighted.

Logic will be to use the Payment Date(from Telema) to be used to calculate the number of days as Payment terms. Use the number with Prefix “NET_” to derive the Payment Terms ref id in Workday. 

Example: 

Payment Date = 19.09.2022

Invoice Date (or date to be used based on further investigation) = 19.08.2022

Subtract Invoice Date from Payment Date i.e. 19.09.2022 - 19.08.2022 = 30 

Prefix NET_ to the number i.e. NET_30 to be used as ref id for Payment Terms.

“Based on your demand for a legal basis, a new request is attached here, where it has been explained in more detail that there is no obstacle against the GDPR for the disclosure of personal data in the current case.
However, I also want to point out that in terms of legal support for the police to obtain evidence, it is generally expected from private actors that the evidence requested is provided. The police's alternative in other cases is a decision on questioning, house search and seizure.”

The legal basis paragraph available in the documented will be attached below.

“There are at least three different supports for when personal data may be provided to the Police Authority's law enforcement activities; if there is an obligation to provide information according to law, if it is not incompatible with the collecting purpose and if that, after a balance of interests, appears to be necessary for purposes relating to the legitimate interests of the data controller or a third party and unless the registered interests and fundamental rights and freedoms
weighs more.


The police authority has a very strong legitimate interest in processing personal data to fight crime. Even if there is no constitutional obligation to provide information or if it would be incompatible with the collecting purpose to disclose information to the police, disclosure should therefore generally be permitted after a balance of interests in the individual case. This applies regardless of the legal basis used to collect the data. With reference to the privacy legislation, the Police Authority is
prevented from giving a detailed account of the background as the request is explained or why must arise.


The police authority's opinion is thus that in a balance of interests which is made according to Article 6.1 must always take into account the authority's mission to fight crime and that this is an important public interest. The authority has as
responsibility to only request data if there is a concrete need and legal prerequisites for processing the personal data. A private actor can thus, when weighing up interests, always assume that the Police Authority has one such strongly justified interest in taking part in the requested information even if
it cannot be done in detail because of confidentiality.


Worth noting in this context is that confidentiality normally applies to data within the framework of a criminal investigation, i.a. with the support of ch. 18 §§ 1 and 2 as well as
35 ch. Section 1 of the Publicity and Confidentiality Act.
The rules in the EU's data protection regulation (GDPR) thus do not prevent private actors from disclosing personal data to the Police Authority's law enforcement activities. The police authority has the right to process personal data for
crime-fighting purposes with support in ch. 2 Section 1 of the Act (2018:1693) on the police's processing of personal data within the scope of the Criminal Data Act.”

Please find the response below (1) in Estonian; and (2) translation to English as well as you might need to pass on this information to non-Estonian speakers. The guidelines have been written by Estonian law firm Ellex-Raidla - since the content of the advice is that we should not correct the data ourselves, please let me know whether this approach is problematic for us and I will try to investigate further whether there could be arguments to counter the current advice.

Regarding the implementation of the Digital Services Act (DSA) and how we plan to prevent non-complying users to access the platform, I am not sure whether these topics have already been addressed internally (DSA will enter into force in Feb 2024) and what is the plan, this will have to be addressed separately. But here’s the advice:

*In Estonian:*

Antud küsimusel on kaks suuremat tahku – maksuõiguslik ja lepinguõiguslik pool. 

*Maksuõigusliku poole pealt* on Boltil tulenevalt DAC7 direktiivist kohustus koguda ise platvormil osalejate kohta maksuandmeid (sh teha kindlaks nende käibemaksukohustuslaseks olemine), kontrollida nende andmete õigsust ja anda selle kohta MTA-le teavet (Epp kommentaar: MTA ehk Eesti Maksu- ja Tolliamet, Euroopa levelil mistahes vastutav maksuamet). Sellest tulenevalt peab Bolt MTA suunal igal juhul trader’ite (autojuhid, restoranid) maksustaatuse kohta andmeid kontrollima ja veenduma äriregistri baasil, et need on korrektsed. 

Sellest eraldiseisev küsimus on see, et kui süsteemis on maksuandmed valed ning suhtluses MTA-ga on Bolt pidanud andmed ise parandama, siis kas sellise parandamise tulemusena tuleks muudatus sisse viia ka Bolti enda süsteemi. *Näeme, et kui Bolt hakkaks ise trader’ite poolt sisestatud andmeid parandama, kaasneksid sellega arvestatavad riskid. Üldine põhimõte peaks olema see, et Bolt on platvormi operaatorina üksnes infoühiskonnateenuse pakkuja ning andmeid platvormile sisestavad üksnes trader’id, mitte platvorm ise.* Sama hakkab kinnitama ka 2024.a veebruaris jõustuv *Digital Services Act (DSA) – Art 6* kohaselt *kui infoühiskonnateenuse pakkuja avastab, et platvormil on avaldatud ebaõiget teavet, tuleb infoühiskonnateenuse pakkujal teavitada konkreetset trader’it probleemist ning takistada tema juurdepääs platvormile seni kuni trader on ise andmed parandanud. Nagu mainitud, siis DSA ei ole küll veel hetkel jõustunud, kuid isegi ilma selle regulatsioonita on olemas risk, et kui Bolt hakkaks ebaõigeid andmeid trader’ite eest ise parandama, tekib argument öelda, et Bolt käsitleb neid andmeid enda andmetena, ning sellisel juhul ei oleks Bolt enam hosting-teenuse pakkuja ega kvalifitseeruks infoühiskonnateenuse pakkujaks, sh ei saaks Bolt tugineda vastutuse piirangutele ja välistustele selle eest, mida trader’id platvormil teevad.* 

Seetõttu soovitaksime konkreetseid trader’eid teavitada sellest, et nad on süsteemis esitanud ebaõigeid andmeid, ning keelata nende juurdepääs süsteemile seni kuni nad on andmed parandanud – see aitaks võimalikult kiiresti vähendada ka erinevusi selle vahel, et süsteemis olev teave on erinev MTA-le edastatavast teabest. Õigusliku aluse selleks annavad ka praegused T&C-d (erakorraline kasutamise peatamine kui trader rikub lepingut). 

Alternatiivselt, kui Bolt soovib ebaõigeid andmeid ise parandada, tuleks arvestada, et trader’eid tuleb sellest igal juhul teavitada, *ning sellisel juhul suureneb risk, et Bolti ei saa pidada hosting-teenuse pakkujaks (kuna infoühiskonnateenuse pakkujaks olemist hinnatakse paljude väikeste kriteeriumite alusel, siis andmete omaalgatuslik parandamine oleks üks täiendav argument, mis kaalukaussi Bolti kahjuks kallutaks). Selleks, et neid riske pigem vähendada, soovitaksimegi teil paluda trader’itel andmed ise ära parandada.*  



*In English:*

There are two major aspects to this issue - tax and contract law.



On the *tax side*, under the DAC7 Directive, Bolt has an obligation to collect tax data (including VAT identification) on the platform participants, to verify the accuracy of these data and to provide information to the tax authority. Consequently, Bolt must in any case check the tax status of traders (drivers, restaurants) with the tax authority and verify that it is correct on the basis of the business register.



A separate question is whether, if the tax data in the system is incorrect and Bolt has had to correct the data itself in its dealings with the tax authority, the result of such a correction should be reflected in Bolt's own system. *We can see that there would be considerable risks if Bolt itself were to correct the data entered by traders.* *The general principle should be that Bolt, as a platform operator, is only an information society service provider and that only traders, not the platform itself, enter data into the platform.* This will be confirmed by the Digital Services Act (DSA), which will come into force in *February 2024* - *Art 6 of the DSA* states that *if an information society service provider discovers that incorrect information has been published on a platform, the information society service provider must notify the individual trader of the problem and prevent the trader from accessing the platform until the trader has corrected the information. As mentioned, the DSA is not yet in force, but even without its regulation there is a risk that if Bolt were to correct the incorrect data for traders itself, there would be an argument that Bolt treats the data as its own, in which case Bolt would no longer be a hosting provider and would not qualify as an ISP, including that Bolt would not be able to rely on the limitations and exclusions of liability for what traders do on the platform.*

We would therefore recommend that individual traders be informed that they have submitted incorrect information to the system and be denied access to the system until they have corrected the information - this would also help to reduce as quickly as possible the discrepancy between the information in the system being different to the information reported to the tax authority. The legal basis for this is also provided by the current T&Cs (emergency suspension of use if trader breaches contract).

Alternatively, if Bolt wishes to correct incorrect data itself, it should be noted that traders must be informed in any case, and *in such a case there is an increased risk that Bolt would not be considered as a hosting service provider (since the assessment of being an information society service provider is based on a number of small criteria, self-correction of data would be an additional argument that would tilt the balance against Bolt). To mitigate these risks, we would suggest that you ask traders to correct the data themselves.*

For Purchase Orders that we raise via Workday, we are the customer and the supplier delivers us the goods/services requested. This then means that all POs we produce in system will have a reference like PO-EE003-23-000001.

However, if you look on the other side of the fence - Bolt might be the supplier to a business. Which means that if we are supplying someone with some goods/services, they may create a Purchase Order (internally in their own ERP system) that they provide to us this could be such as PO-1234. This would then be reflected on our customer invoice, so we want our customers to pay, and we as the suppliers receive the money. 

Therefore I think it makes sense to still include PO number, because the customer could give us their PO so when we issue out the invoice to them, they have a reference in their system for 3-way matching. 😉

It may of course help the fleet to be better under the radar of the Romanian tax authorities and maybe avoid paying VAT but this is not something that we should be encouraging.

Hey [~accountid:641d70192cee496759ec78f0]! 

What I see here is that “delete an account” and “delete my personal data” are different things. When the user requests to delete their data, we should delete it unless we have other reasons not to do so (legal obligation, legal claim, or ongoing purpose to process this data like collecting emails for fraud prevention in our legitimate interest (if we stated this in our Privacy Policy before collecting this data for this purpose)). When the user requests to delete an account, the data can be scheduled for deletion, for example, but it’s not a request to delete data. The deletion of their data is triggered by us in this case since we no longer have a purpose to keep this info.

*What I propose:*
1. Firstly, we should make it clear for the user and ask the user if the user would like to delete his personal data from Bolt app, whether we can consider this request as a data deletion request. If that’s the case, we proceed under the basis of right to erasure. So we need to delete all his data from our systems, including account, and leave the data we need to keep (steps 2-3).
2. Secondly, the CS Team can follow their policies on account deletion until the user makes a request to delete their data or we see that the request is actually about data deletion. So we should follow step one, and until we get a response that the user wants to delete his data, we cannot advice on this to the CS team, in my view. So they can say that the account cannot be deleted since there are ongoing issues with their activity.
3. According to our [Romanian Privacy policy |https://bolt.eu/en/legal/ro/privacy-for-riders/]we can keep some data for investigating fraud. If the user makes a request to delete their data, we have to identify what data the CS Team needs to keep to investigate this fraud and keep them, and the rest of the data should be deleted since we do not have purposes to keep them (unless we have a legal obligation or claims to defence).


What are your thoughts on data deletion and account deletion? 
What is the process once the account is deleted? Do we schedule the deletion and does the user have a right to restore their account once it’s deleted? Because deletion of the data does not give opportunity to restore it in our systems.

I added some comments to the rationale sent by the partner- can you please share them with the partner? I’d be however more than willing to have a call with partner’s privacy representative to discuss this- maybe it would be more efficient. 

_The Bolt platform on which the personal data of customers and couriers are located is a platform belonging to Bolt and Bolt is responsible for its proper operation in terms of IT processes and its proper protection, including in the event of a personal data leak._

*Comment*: This is correct. Bolt is providing information society services and in this capacity acts as an independent data controller. Those processing operations are not subject to the agreement with partners and therefore are not covered by the data sharing schedule. Additionally, most of the data collected via platform is not shared with the partners.

_It is customers and couriers who log on to the Bolt platform to place orders and provide delivery services. It is Bolt that collects all customer data and creates their database. We, as a Partner, use this data to the extent necessary to sell our goods. We understand that during the execution of the order, e.g. the courier's telephone number is made available to us, this is how Bolt works, but this does not mean that we are the administrator of personal data collected on your platform, but a processor. This is also the model of cooperation we have adopted with other Bolt competitors and we ask that you adopt this model in cooperation with you._

*Comment*: Customers and couriers that use the platform are offered information society services by Bolt, i.e. the option to use the app which acts as a marketplace. Please note that Bolt is neither a party to the deliver agreement (this is concluded by and between end-user and the courier) nor to the sale agreement (this is concluded by and between end-user and the partner). Given the actual set up and provision of Bolt Food Platform Terms and Conditions, Bolt is not the seller of the goods or provider of the delivery services and is not liable in any way for the performance of the agreements related to them. By operating the Bolt Food Platform, Bolt acts as the agent for the partners in relation to mediation of sales agreements between the partners and the clients (similarly Bolt also acts as the agent for the couriers). Please note that Bolt doesn’t demonstrate its own purposes in terms of processing operations carried out by the partner that lead to conclusion of the sales agreement - Bolt is only a commercial agent and it is a partner as a party to the agreement that processes end-user’s data on its own behalf. We also appreciate that there may be various legal obligations that may oblige the partner to store the data for its own purposes (e.g. stemming from tax/accounting legislation). Neither Bolt nor partner restaurants process data on behalf of other party- both parties need and use personal data in the course of their own service provision making them separate controllers of personal data.

Summary of issues:

A Driver has had 3 complaints from 3 different Riders lodged against him during their time with Bolt.

Dudley, as the licensing Council, has been informed of the complaints. They have not been provided with the Rider’s personal data.

Dudley Council have requested the personal data of the Riders so they can conduct their own investigation. Bolt has refused to provide this due to not being able to meet our Article 6 GDPR requirements. Consent has been sought from all 3 Riders, 1 Rider has provided consent and their details have been provided to the Council.

Dudley Council is adamant they are entitled to the information through their licensing agreement and continue to request the 3 Rider’s personal data.

To date, Bolt has been unable to gather consent from 2 of the 3 Riders and therefore their data has not been released to the police.

----

We have reviewed and re-reviewed this issue. It is still clear that the Council have not provided us with an Article 6 GDPR basis for the data they have requested. Further, we have already approached the Riders for their consent. We do not want to appear to be circumnavigating a Rider who has declined to provide consent. This will open up issues both publicly and with GDPR. 

The Council has provided us with a DPA which has satisfied all concerns we have other that our Article 6 obligations.

----

Possible actions:

* Continue to approach the 2 Riders who made complaints and we have not been able to gather consent from.
* Explain to the Council our position once again and advise without consent we will not be providing details.
* Advise the Council we have continued to try to contact the Riders and since we have not been able to gain consent we now consider the matter closed.

I believe our best course here is to re-iterate that the Council’s right to process data is not the same as our duty to disclose the data they have requested. the Council have provided us with plenty of rationale for their right to process, but nothing to satisfy our duty to protect the data we hold.

We can also reiterate to the Council that we will continue to reach out to the Riders and request that they provide their consent so we may pass this on. Since we have already requested consent, unless there is a major development then this is the only appropriate legal basis.

Replace lines 13 and beyond in [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/martech/models/ads/etl_driver_lead_marketing_attribution/etl_driver_lead_marketing_attribution.sql|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/martech/models/ads/etl_driver_lead_marketing_attribution/etl_driver_lead_marketing_attribution.sql|smart-link] with below:

{code:sql}WITH last_click AS (
SELECT user_id, MAX(event_timestamp) AS last_timestamp
FROM {{ source("bigquery_spark","ga4_analytics") }}
WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL
AND event_name = 'Driver Signed Up'
GROUP BY user_id
),

first_click AS (
SELECT user_id, MIN(event_timestamp) AS first_timestamp
FROM {{ source("bigquery_spark","ga4_analytics") }}
WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL
AND event_name = 'Driver Signed Up'
GROUP BY user_id
),

driver_source AS (
-- get attribution information from Google Analytics
SELECT
a.user_pseudo_id,
a.user_id,
CASE 
  WHEN a.traffic_source.name IS NULL AND event_params.campaign.string_value IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
  WHEN a.traffic_source.name IS NULL THEN event_params.campaign.string_value
  ELSE a.traffic_source.name
END AS google_analytics_campaign,
CASE 
  WHEN a.traffic_source.medium IS NULL AND event_params.medium.string_value IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
  WHEN a.traffic_source.medium IS NULL THEN event_params.medium.string_value
  ELSE a.traffic_source.medium
END AS google_analytics_medium,
CASE 
  WHEN a.traffic_source.source IS NULL AND event_params.source.string_value IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
  WHEN a.traffic_source.source IS NULL THEN event_params.source.string_value
  WHEN a.traffic_source.source = '(direct)' THEN 'organic'
  ELSE a.traffic_source.source
END AS google_analytics_source
FROM
{{ source("bigquery_spark","ga4_analytics") }} as a
INNER JOIN
last_click as b -- If we want to change our model, we just need to modify here
ON b.user_id =  a.user_id
AND b.last_timestamp = a.event_timestamp
WHERE
a.event_name = 'Driver Signed Up'
),

attribution AS (
-- append user attribution information from driver_source to the individual Driver Signed Up event in Google Analytics
SELECT
a.event_timestamp as google_analytics_timestamps,
a.user_pseudo_id as google_analytics_id,
a.user_id,
split_part(a.user_id,'lead-driver-',2) as hash,
c.google_analytics_campaign,
c.google_analytics_medium,
c.google_analytics_source,
a.event_name AS google_analytics_event_name,
b.last_timestamp
FROM
{{ source("bigquery_spark","ga4_analytics") }} as a
INNER JOIN
last_click as b
ON a.user_id =  b.user_id
AND b.last_timestamp = a.event_timestamp
LEFT JOIN driver_source as c
ON a.user_id = c.user_id
WHERE
a.event_name = 'Driver Signed Up'
),

appsflyer_attribution AS (
SELECT
split_part(customer_user_id, '-', 3) AS hash,
appsflyer_id,
DATE_TRUNC('day', CASE
WHEN media_source IN ('restricted', 'organic') THEN install_time
WHEN attributed_touch_time IS NULL THEN install_time
ELSE attributed_touch_time END) AS attributed_touch_date_original,
CASE WHEN media_source = 'restricted' THEN 'impression'
ELSE attributed_touch_type END AS attributed_touch_type,
install_time,
event_time,
CASE
WHEN media_source IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
WHEN media_source LIKE '%influencer%' THEN 'BAP'
WHEN media_source LIKE '%ambassador%' THEN 'BAP'
WHEN media_source = 'googleadwords_int' THEN 'Google Ads'
WHEN media_source IN ('Facebook Ads','restricted') THEN 'Facebook Ads'
WHEN media_source IN ('Email') THEN 'Mailing campaigns'
WHEN media_source IN ('social') THEN 'External channels'
WHEN media_source = 'bytedanceglobal_int' THEN 'TikTok'
WHEN media_source = 'snapchat_int' THEN 'Snapchat'
WHEN media_source LIKE 'invite%' THEN 'Invites'
ELSE media_source
END AS original_media_source,
media_source AS unprocessed_media_source,
CASE
WHEN contributor_1_media_source IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
WHEN contributor_1_media_source LIKE '%influencer%' THEN 'BAP'
WHEN contributor_1_media_source LIKE '%ambassador%' THEN 'BAP'
WHEN contributor_1_media_source = 'googleadwords_int' THEN 'Google Ads'
WHEN contributor_1_media_source IN ('Facebook Ads','restricted') THEN 'Facebook Ads'
WHEN contributor_1_media_source = 'bytedanceglobal_int' THEN 'TikTok'
WHEN contributor_1_media_source = 'snapchat_int' THEN 'Snapchat'
WHEN contributor_1_media_source LIKE 'invite%' THEN 'Invites'
ELSE contributor_1_media_source
END AS attributed_1_contributor,
CASE WHEN media_source = 'restricted' THEN 'Unknown Facebook channel'
ELSE af_channel
END AS channel,
campaign,
af_c_id AS campaign_id,
af_adset AS adset,
af_adset_id AS adset_id,
af_keywords AS keywords,
country_code,
app_id,
CASE
WHEN app_id = 'id897442736' THEN 'iOS'
WHEN app_id = 'ee.mtakso.driver' THEN 'Android'
END AS install_os
FROM
{{ source("appsflyer","inapps") }}
WHERE
event_date >= DATE('2022-01-01')
AND event_name = 'Driver Signed Up'
AND customer_user_id LIKE 'lead-driver-%%'
),

/*
We create a temporal table, in order to get a previous transformation
to organize our data and filter by period and event type need it.
*/

mapping_analytics AS (
SELECT
COALESCE(google_analytics_source, 'unknown') AS google_analytics_source,
COALESCE(google_analytics_medium, 'unknown') AS google_analytics_medium,
assigned_channel AS map_assigned_channel
FROM {{ source("ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark","mapping_analytics_and_appsflyer") }}
GROUP BY 1,2,3
),

driver_lead_marketing_attribution AS (
SELECT
google_analytics_id,
appsflyer_id,
COALESCE(fdrl.hash, driver_attribution_google_analytics.hash, appsflyer_attribution.hash) AS lead_hash,
fdrl.id AS lead_driver_id,
fdrl.created AS lead_created,
fdrl.source AS lead_portal_source,

attributed_touch_date_original AS appsflyer_attributed_touch_date_original,
attributed_touch_type AS appsflyer_attributed_touch_type,

install_time as appsflyer_install_time,
event_time as appsflyer_event_time,
google_analytics_timestamps,

google_analytics_campaign,
campaign AS appsflyer_campaign,
campaign_id AS appsflyer_campaign_id,

COALESCE(google_analytics_medium, 'unknown') AS google_analytics_medium,
channel AS appsflyer_channel,

COALESCE(original_media_source, 'unknown') AS appsflyer_original_media_source ,
COALESCE(unprocessed_media_source, 'unknown') AS appsflyer_unprocessed_media_source,
COALESCE(google_analytics_source, 'unknown') AS google_analytics_source,

attributed_1_contributor AS appsflyer_attributed_1_contributor,

adset AS appsflyer_adset,
adset_id AS appsflyer_adset_id,
keywords AS appsflyer_keywords,
country_code AS appsflyer_country_code,
app_id AS appsflyer_app_id,
install_os AS appsflyer_install_os

FROM
{{ source("ng_public_spark","fleet_driver_registration_log") }} AS fdrl
FULL OUTER JOIN
attribution AS driver_attribution_google_analytics
ON fdrl.hash = driver_attribution_google_analytics.hash
FULL OUTER JOIN appsflyer_attribution
ON fdrl.hash = appsflyer_attribution.hash
WHERE fdrl.created >= DATE('2022-01-01')
),
/*
We create two temporal tables, in order to apply COALESCE to both queries.
Also to avoid a triple join with rules pointing to different tables.
*/

pre_final AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT 
    driver_lead_marketing_attribution.*,
    COALESCE(
    CASE
    WHEN driver_lead_marketing_attribution.appsflyer_original_media_source IS NULL THEN mapping_analytics.map_assigned_channel
    WHEN driver_lead_marketing_attribution.appsflyer_original_media_source = 'unknown' THEN mapping_analytics.map_assigned_channel
    WHEN driver_lead_marketing_attribution.appsflyer_original_media_source = 'organic' THEN mapping_analytics.map_assigned_channel
    ELSE driver_lead_marketing_attribution.appsflyer_original_media_source
    END, 'Organic') AS combined_channel,
    cast(COALESCE( from_unixtime(google_analytics_timestamps/1000000), lead_created ) AS date) AS lead_created_date

    FROM driver_lead_marketing_attribution
    LEFT JOIN mapping_analytics
    ON driver_lead_marketing_attribution.google_analytics_source
    = mapping_analytics.google_analytics_source
    AND driver_lead_marketing_attribution.google_analytics_medium
    = mapping_analytics.google_analytics_medium
)


SELECT 
lead_hash,
lead_created,
min_by(appsflyer_adset, lead_created) AS appsflyer_adset,
min_by(appsflyer_adset_id, lead_created) AS appsflyer_adset_id,
min_by(appsflyer_app_id, lead_created) AS appsflyer_app_id,
min_by(appsflyer_attributed_1_contributor, lead_created) AS appsflyer_attributed_1_contributor,
min_by(appsflyer_attributed_touch_date_original, lead_created) AS appsflyer_attributed_touch_date_original,
min_by(appsflyer_attributed_touch_type, lead_created) AS appsflyer_attributed_touch_type,
min_by(appsflyer_campaign, lead_created) AS appsflyer_campaign,
min_by(appsflyer_campaign_id, lead_created) AS appsflyer_campaign_id,
min_by(appsflyer_channel, lead_created) AS appsflyer_channel,
min_by(appsflyer_country_code, lead_created) AS appsflyer_country_code,
min_by(appsflyer_event_time, lead_created) AS appsflyer_event_time,
min_by(appsflyer_id, lead_created) AS appsflyer_id,
min_by(appsflyer_install_os, lead_created) AS appsflyer_install_os,
min_by(appsflyer_install_time, lead_created) AS appsflyer_install_time,
min_by(appsflyer_keywords, lead_created) AS appsflyer_keywords,
min_by(appsflyer_original_media_source, lead_created) AS appsflyer_original_media_source,
min_by(appsflyer_unprocessed_media_source, lead_created) AS appsflyer_unprocessed_media_source,
min_by(combined_channel, lead_created) AS combined_channel,
min_by(google_analytics_campaign, lead_created) AS google_analytics_campaign,
min_by(google_analytics_id, lead_created) AS google_analytics_id,
min_by(google_analytics_medium, lead_created) AS google_analytics_medium,
min_by(google_analytics_source, lead_created) AS google_analytics_source,
min_by(google_analytics_timestamps, lead_created) AS google_analytics_timestamps,
min_by(lead_created_date, lead_created) AS lead_created_date,
min_by(lead_driver_id, lead_created) AS lead_driver_id,
min_by(lead_portal_source, lead_created) AS lead_portal_source,
current_timestamp() AS _last_ingested
FROM pre_final

{% if is_incremental() %}
WHERE 
  lead_created_date >= date_sub(date'{{ var("data_interval_start") }}', 35)
{% endif %} 

GROUP BY 1,2{code}
