Hi [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3] - interesting circumstances! I’ve gone to town a bit here because you can take this sort of approach over to other tickets.

----

*You can give the business two options: take a view and pay it, noting it’s a cost over 18 or so months. Or, you can spend a very limited amount of time helping them deal with the licensor based on the below (i.e. offer to help with one email). Then it’s up to them on their time to settle it because it’s too low value for legal to spend significant time on (the charge is around £50ish a month).*

Overall, I think it’s OK for expediency to arrange to pay this as is - although ideally we first get some clarity from the licensor or the water company on how this has been apportioned to us.

Principles:

The wording of the licence is standard terrible license wording, but it is clearly intended to reflect a standard, ‘service charge’-like arrangement whereby Bolt is responsible for paying its fair share towards services that are *_incurred by the licensor_*, with the exception being business rates liability which we are supposedly paying directly.

Surface water run-off charges are generally considered to be a ‘service’ - obviously it’s debatable whether that’s covered in this licence.

It’s fair for service costs (such as electricity) to be split between licensees, but this license gives no mention of the same charges being payable in respect of the upkeep of the Centre. Indeed, the agreement makes it clear that the *_licensor_* is *_responsible_* for the maintenance and upkeep of the Centre - with no express mention to the passthrough of costs. 

Ultimately, there are two reasonable outcomes:
- we pay a fair share for water drainage services incurred by the licensor in respect of *_our Unit_*_._
- we pay a fair share for water drainage services directly in respect of *_our Unit_*_._

This bill appears to give no reference to our Unit. Which begs the question, *how is this being apportioned?*

We do need to consider that we have a commercial relationship with the licensor that presumably we want to maintain.

If the business *_does_* want to make a fuss of this, you can offer to ghostwrite some friendly messaging along the following lines (but then they are on their own and need to sort it):

- As a headline, Bolt is comfortable with contributing towards some run off costs, but at present this does not appear to be correct.
- The licence says that they are responsible for the upkeep and maintenance of the centre. We have no interest in property in the land in the unit or the centre. Therefore the licensor is responsible for incurring costs in respect of the centre (note clause 8 and also the wording in clause 2: “… the cost to _Us_ of supplying _You_ with the services.”)
- With that in mind, it doesn’t make sense that this has been addressed to us. This bill also doesn’t appear to be addressed to our unit but instead the whole business park - so it’s not clear how this is being apportioned. Bolt shouldn’t be paying costs in respect of the whole centre. Do they have any knowledge of how this has happened? Can they please contact the water company to sort this out, noting they are responsible for this in the licence? If not, we will need to get in touch with the water company directly to say we’re picking this up with them. 

Then add some bonus comment to say happy to come to an arrangement but we need to make sure it’s proper and fair, please.

* "Cron ran more than the warning time"

* "Cron got more rows than warning limit"
** Reason: {{limit_warning}} is not configured, and it's default is {{limit*70%}}, however, the cron will process a maximum of {{limit}} rows, no more.
** Solution: Configure {{limit_warning}} to {{limit}}, because the cron will process a maximum of {{limit}} rows.

If the water company itself has a bee in its bonnet that *_we_* should be paying, and they say that we need to pay as occupiers, then it’s obviously not worth protracted back and forth to sort it out - we should just pay it. Of course, that’s a slightly different point to making sure the apportionment is correct/fair.

At the same time, I note the licensor have said that water costs are included (according to the posts in this ticket). It is a bit silly for them to say that water is included but run off charges are not. As per my first post, they are contractually responsible for upkeep of the centre etc.

On that note, if there is any express suggestion in the documentation / emails that the rates payable are fully inclusive of all utilities / costs / services, then if we do pay the water company directly, we could ask from a rebate from the licensor as they hadn’t made it clear anywhere that these sorts of ‘private estate run off charges would’ apply to us (noting that these charges are not incurred by virtue of our occupation - they would have been charged anyway). This is not a leading suggestion, I’m just point out the range of things we could do. All things considered, as these costs are fairly low nobody is going to want to spend a lot of time over this… but if the circumstances are right and we were represented that fees were fully inclusive, we could ask. It would be too impractical and complicated to try and legally enforce this though as it’s not open/shut. It’s also the sort of thing that is likely to cause annoyance - nagging them for money that they aren’t bang to rights to compensate us for.

Hey! Posting here also our current approach for context to discuss in the call:

* The product team have confirmed that they would be able to provide us with the file, however they would not be able to modify it.
* The right to access (DSAR) is not an absolute right. There may be circumstances where export of certain data would not be justified. If we have the recording which would contain also personal data of third parties and it is technically impossible\unreasonably difficult to cut it out \hash it, then we would have strong grounds to decline the export. Otherwise we may be in a situation of a data breach by disclosing personal data unlawfully. 
* Therefore, at least in the beginning when the feature is new, we would prefer to have specific requests for the recording to be escalated to the privacy team (via SD).
* If we file is deleted and we do not have it in our systems anymore, then we don’t have to be able to export it since this right only applies to personal data we hold.
* On the police requests - we will discuss in the call and later confirm in the ticket the approach for now. 
* Also, rephrasing what Mirjam posted earlier here “Advertising this feature by claiming we’re 100% GDPR compliant - “*should not be done at all”.* We don’t want to attract any unwanted attention.

We will have to fall back on general consumer legislation which in Finland is the Consumer Protection Act (20.1.1978/38) and the principle is that the consumer has a right to be refunded to the payment method that was originally used. Businesses can offer refunds to vouchers or similar but the consumer will ultimately  still have the right to receive a refund to the initial payment method. 

To sum up the advice, Bolt should: 

# Offer BB refund of the relevant amount. 
# If consumer refuses to receive BB refund, offer partial refund to original payment method. 
# If partial refund to original payment method isn’t possible for some practical reason, offer full refund to initial payment method. 

This ticket will now be closed but please reach out if you need additional advice and we can then reopen the ticket.

Best regards, 

Michelle

Users can initiate an automatic deletion process (via the relevant self-help article), therefore they can delete their profiles without contacting the Support Team. 

Usually they can’t delete their accounts automatically if they have a pending price review or a failed payment etc. In these cases our system rejects the deletion request. However, if there’s a scheduled block (a blocking that is conducted manually by CS agents) on their account, the system still allows them to delete their profile. 

This is a problem, because in several markets we usually put a scheduled block on riders who didn’t pay for their ride. This way they can delete their account and create a new one, so 10 minutes later they can order another Bolt ride without settling their debt towards the affected drivers. This can be really demotivating and disappointing to drivers who experience that a rider who didn’t pay for the service can order via the application a few days later. 

My question is: what do you think, would it be possible to ask our technical team to include these manual schedule blockings into the deletion eligibility check so riders couldn’t delete their account via a self-help article if there’s a schedule block on their profile? h3. {color:#ff5630}Problems and opportunities{color}

* Not all of our content aligns with our Content Policies
** Additionally, content policies are based on the idea that self-help should solve user issues, whereas the CSP team have found that most issues cannot be solved by articles ([source|https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1M2-Oibgsapsy635of1fHrOBDH4ZF0ZVy493_iiGvspc/edit#slide=id.g2502adde039_0_52])
** We are increasingly being asked to include content to cover issues such as pricing and other rapidly changing information, usually by Ops teams, who have nowhere else to store the information
* External KB articles contain a wide range of topics, not all of which are directly related to solving a user issue or question
* The in-app UX for self-help has changed (see [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/GMTJ8PSS2/p1686147244983599]) meaning we will need to ensure that the self-help articles align with this update
* We need to organise our content the same way as is done on [http://bolt.eu|http://bolt.eu|smart-link] , so that we can display the correct information based on the user’s location and language. The current organisation is based on limitations with Zendesk
* Content mastersheets are messy, outdated, and don’t help with mapping content.
** We currently rely on google sheets, but we haven’t explored the possibilities that GitHub has in terms of managing content
* We do not have a review system in place for monitoring the accuracy of and need for our content

----

h3. {color:#abf5d1}Desired outcomes{color}

* We have reviewed and confirmed the content policies are still relevant, and if not we have updated them
* The content in the KB aligns with our content policies, and is future-proofed against developments by CSP
* We have mapped content by issue type so that we can identify content that does not solve common user issues that are dealt with by CS
* A proposal on what to do with non CS-issue content is created (so that it can be presented to product teams
* Content mastersheets allow the team to filter by specific elements so the team can quickly find articles with specific information when needed
* The KB style guide is updated (i.e. it includes GitHub info instead of ZD)
* KB articles are updated according to the revised KB style guide
* The external KB content is organised into the correct country and language folders so it can be displayed correctly on the website

----

h3. Deliverables

* A document mapping all self-help content to current issue tags
* KB style guide is updated with Github information
* New content mastersheets are created
* KB localisations file is updated with the new folder structure for languages (matching the web locale)

----

h3. Out of scope

* Proposal for where to store content that is not related to solving user issues (e.g. informative, rapidly changing info like pricing) 
* Github useability improvements
